meta.unit: EUR bn, current prices; USD converted at ECB annual average (2026 = Jan-Aug mean) as in trade_full.json
meta.years: 2021 = pre-war level; 2022-2025 full years; 2026 = January-August only
meta.list: Common High Priority List (CHPL), version of 23 Feb 2024, 50 HS-6 codes (EU/US/UK/Japan); same list applied to all years for comparability
meta.measure: Shipping-country view: value of CHPL goods each country (customs territory) shipped to Russia. Central = own export records adjusted toward what Russian customs recorded as dispatched from that country (KSE 2023 calibration) where that comparison exists. Low = own export records. High = allowance for under-recording and misdeclared codes.
meta.role: Display marker only. All of these goods are already inside each country's exports_to_RUS in trade_full.json (or residual/reexports for adjusted parts); do NOT add to totals.
meta.change_definition: change_vs_2021_eur_bn_2022_2026 = sum over 2022-2025 of (central - central 2021) + (central 2026 Jan-Aug - 8/12 of central 2021).
meta.certainty_scale: A = own customs data, small gaps; B = own data with moderate mirror gap or partial estimation; C = large mirror gap or hub with no customs cross-check; D = educated guess.

brand_origin.what: Estimated value of CHPL goods reaching Russia by the country where the PRODUCING COMPANY is headquartered (brand origin), all shipping routes combined. SEPARATE from the shipping-country marker; do not add the two.
brand_origin.anchor: KSE Institute & Yermak-McFaul group (Jan 2024), Russian transaction-level customs data Jan-Oct 2023, 45 CHP codes (USD 8.77bn): producer HQ US 25.5%, EU 6.1%, Taiwan 7.0%, other coalition 5.4%, China 41.0%, other 7.0%, unknown 8.0% (unknown spread pro rata here). Country of manufacture: China 63.1%, coalition 20.9%. Top producers: Intel, Huawei, Analog Devices, AMD, Texas Instruments, Lenovo, IBM, Dell, Hikvision, STMicro.
notes: 2023 is the only year with a published value-weighted producer split. Other years are EDUCATED GUESSES.
2021: before the war most Western-brand goods were shipped directly from Western countries (EU states alone shipped EUR 3.8bn of the EUR ~10.7bn).

2024-2026: China's share of shipments rose to 75-85% (KSE Q2 2026); The Insider (Apr 2025) found Western-brand electronics via China down ~17x and Intel via third countries from USD 235m (2023) to 7m (2024) in Russian customs data, but Russia restricted customs-data publication from spring 2024, so part of that fall is invisibility, not a real cut. KSE Q2 2026 still sees Hong Kong carrying processors and other ICs, likely coalition-made.
Splits inside the EU and 'other coalition' (Korea, Japan, Switzerland incl. STMicroelectronics per KSE, UK) are guesses from KSE's company lists; treat member-state numbers as illustrative only.

Battlefield count evidence (not value): 95% of ~2,800 foreign parts in Russian weapons came from coalition-HQ producers, 72% US (KSE/Yermak-McFaul, Jan 2024); RUSI 'Silicon Lifeline' (Nov 2022) found >450 foreign components, mostly US brands.

sources.what: research/2026-10/gaps/trade_full.json: FX, total exports to Russia used for 2026 Jan-Aug scaling and gap years

notes: Display marker only: every euro here is already inside exports_to_RUS (trade_full.json) or the residual/re-export layers. Do not add to totals.
Shipping-country view is primary (the country that let the goods leave). brand_origin is a separate, overlapping view of the same money; never add the two.

The same 50-code list (Feb 2024) is applied to all years, including 2021-2023 when it was not yet in force. HS2017 predecessors used for 2021 reports: 880330->880730, 854150->854159, 852580->852589, 854890->854800; 854149 has no clean HS2017 equivalent and is missing for 2021 (small).

Central values move each exporter's own record toward what Russian customs recorded as dispatched from it in Jan-Oct 2023 (KSE). Factors: China 1.25, Hong Kong 2.96, Turkiye 2.99, UAE 1.59, other non-EAEU 1.3 (raw 2.0, damped because part of KSE's 'other' belongs to non-reporters), EAEU 1.0 (no customs border, no Russian cross-check), EU/coalition 1.0 with the residual shown separately. 2021 factor 1.0 (Russia's own 2021 records match the partner sum). 2022 = midpoint. The 2023 factor is carried to 2024-2026: EDUCATED GUESS.

Unallocated residuals in 2023: about EUR 0.17bn dispatched from EU territory and EUR 0.17bn from other coalition territory in Russian records, beyond what those countries report. The coalition residual is assigned to Taiwan (not in Comtrade); the EU residual is not assigned to member states.

2026 = January-August. EU from Eurostat monthly data; Hong Kong from its monthly Comtrade data (Jan-Jul x 8/7); all others = 2025 x (Jan-Aug 2026 / 2025 total exports to Russia from trade_full.json), range x0.8-1.25.
Belarus and Taiwan are educated guesses (certainty D). Iran, North Korea and Belarusian factory output under other codes are not covered by CHPL codes; see china_military, arms and belarus files.

Russian imports by origin in 2021 (Russia's own Comtrade report) show China-made CHPL goods worth EUR 5.0bn against China's own shipments of EUR 3.3bn: before the war a third of Chinese-made CHPL goods reached Russia via third countries.

Hong Kong's gap: HK trade statistics exclude transshipment cargo, and HK traders sell goods that ship from mainland warehouses; Russian customs record HK as dispatch country. That is why the HK central is ~3x HK's own figure. Low case = HK's own figure.

India 2024 is dominated by processing units/servers (847150, EUR 0.39bn reported); Malaysia 2022-2024 by bearings (848210); UAE by aircraft/UAV parts (880730) and network gear (851762); Kazakhstan by cylindrical bearings (848250) and network gear; Turkiye by switching apparatus (853690) and CNC machines.
